notes:
Lead origin: inbound self-serve signup; small-mid SaaS vendor focused on conversational support. Primary persona: Head of Product (Jordan Lee) + Eng lead. Very cost sensitive — clear budget cap for inference (want < $X per 1k tokens) but need quality close to current hosted provider. Key asks:
- Which model family to pick for chat: Llama2 variants vs Mistral vs Qwen?
- Quantized options: acceptable quality loss for 4-bit/8-bit quantization?
- Can we start on a cheaper 7B Mistral/Qwen and bump to 13B Llama variant if quality regresses?
- Latency requirement: median response < 300ms for 300-token prompts; p95 < 800ms. Typical prompt size ~200-400 tokens.
- Throughput: initial peak ~15-20 rps, expecting to scale to ~50 rps in 6 months if retention improves.
- Multilingual KB (EN + ES): tokenization differences flagged; requests whether model family affects token counts and cost predictability.
- Safety/hallucination: need examples of hallucination rates across models and recommended eval prompts.
- Integration ask: can we switch model variants w/o app changes (routing/fallback recommended)?

Quoted snippets from calls: "We want the cheapest model that 'just works' for multi-step support dialogs"; "If we can shave 30% off token costs without UX regression we're interested".

POC plan proposed: run hosted-api POC for 2 weeks using 3 variants (Mistral-7B-8x, Llama-13B-std, Qwen-7B) with identical prompt templates and telemetry to compare latency, token cost, and quality (NPS & false-resolution rate). SE asked for a cost-per-1k-tokens estimate and expected median latency for each variant.

Notes on decision criteria (from customer): quality > latency for final deploy but early POC can optimize for cost. SSO + SOC2 are must-haves before contract. Data retention/retention_controls question: want 30-day delete policy and audit log.

Next steps logged: set up POC project in account, provide a small script to replay 500 historical support dialogs (customer to provide sanitized dataset), produce a modeled cost/latency table and suggested default routing policy (cheap model with automatic fallback to higher-quality model on failed confidence).
